findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed ice scoop handle to be in contact with ice in ice machine. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was moved to an approved location. Ensure ice scoop is not in contact with ice to prevent any possible contaminantion.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS foods being kept in walk in cooler that were kept longer than there 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed 2 clean ladles to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, ladles were pulled and put through the wash, rinse, sanitize process. Ensure all utensils are properly cleaned to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS foods being kept in walk in cooler that were kept longer than there 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed street corn dip to be thawing in the basin of the triple sink. Discussed with PIC, inspector provided proper thawing education and dip was submerged under running water. Ensure when thawing items are kept submerged under running water or in a cooler.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the inside top of a microwave and the outside of a toaster to be soiled with food accumulation. Discussed with PIC, both surfaces were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents food accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the shelves in the walk in cooler to have an accumulation of dust and food debris present. Discussed with PIC, ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents contamination. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed two employees to improperly wash hands. Hands were adequately washed with water, lathering with soap, and rinsing; however, no barrier was used to turn off the faucet handles. Inspector discussed with PIC and employees. Ensure staff is aware to correctly wash hands then turn the faucets off with a barrier such as a paper towel in order not to re-contaminate the hands. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sani bucket in the kitchen to be 0 ppm. Discussed with employees. Ensure frequent sani bucket changes in order to maintain concentration. Quaternary ammonium should be 200-400 ppm. Facility has test strips to confirm concentration levels. Employee re-made sani bucket to correct: 400 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following areas in need of cleaning (non-food contact locations):
1. Area behind the oven has significant dust and grease. 
2. Sides of oven and fryers are soiled with grease splash.
3. Interior of ovens are caked with black, burnt food splash.
4. Interior of fryer has a layer of grease and debris.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff forms a schedule to clean the above mentioned areas. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

(REPEAT) Observed thick accumulation of frost and ice build-up on the fan, ceiling, and floor of the walk-in freezer. Bormida has been to the facility to conduct repairs (new motor and fan needed per CFPM). It is an ongoing problem at the facility and they are actively attempting to correct the issue. Repeat violation from last routine inspections on 6/24/22 and 1/17/23. Repair by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of caulking and/or re-caulking: 
1. Mop sink (moldy and black - re-caulk).
2. Dish machine (black and moldy in front of spray nozzle, coming away from wall and equipment as well).
3. Employee bathroom hand sink (coming away from wall and sink - re-caulk).

Discussed repairs with PIC and CFPM. Ensure maintenance staff repairs the above mentioned areas. Correct by next routine inspection. Repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/17/23.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

(REPEAT) Observed the interior baffle of the ice machine to have a thick layer of pink slime/white chunky mold. PIC and employees were shown the mold. Ice machine was being cleaned during the inspection - ice removed, washed, rinsed, sanitized interior. Discussed creating a routine cleaning schedule for the ice machine due to the repeat violation. Repeat from 6/24/22 inspection. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed the reach-in coolers within both wings to lack thermometers. Discussed with PIC. PIC was placing an order for several extra thermometers to have at the facility. Ensure all cold holding units have a thermometer within to verify temperature. Purchase and place in coolers before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

(REPEAT) Observed thick accumulation of frost and ice build-up on the fan, ceiling, and floor of the walk-in freezer. Bormida has been to the facility to conduct repairs. It is an ongoing issue that has taken time to diagnose and rectify. Facility is aware and actively trying to fix the walk-in freezer. Repeat violation from last routine inspection on 6/24/22.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of caulking and/or re-caulking: mop sink (moldy and black - re-caulk), dish machine (black and moldy in front of spray nozzle, coming away from wall and equipment on other side near 3 compartment sink), and employee bathroom hand sink (coming away from sink and wall). Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure maintenance staff conducts repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed both CFPM’s to have expired allergen training certifications. Provided educational handout to re-take the course online. Ensure all certified food protection manager’s complete allergen awareness training and print certificates for employee files in main office. Discussed with PIC. Complete before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

Cucumbers in the walk in cooler are observed with white fuzz (assumed to be mold). PIC was directed to the items and they were discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

There is an accumulation of pink/yellow slime on the deflector shield in the ice machine. Ice is considered a ready to eat (RTE) food and should have emphasis place on its protection from contaminants. PIC was shown the slime and cleaned the item during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Thick accumulations of frost and ice are observed on the shelves, floor and packaging of food items in the walk in freezer. PIC instructed to ensure that they remain free of frost/ice and that cleaning is easily completed.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

On arrival, the sani buckets observed were below effective levels of Quat based sanitizer. Bucket had been recently made at the time of the inspection commencing and had not been sitting long. Investigation shows that the mixing machine does not appear to be holding solution in the lines well, and so is not mixing the correct amounts. Allowing the machine to run for a few moments seems to allow it to pull in affective amounts for making a correct solution. PIC will ensure employees are aware of this requirement until service can be completed on the machine. EcoLab has been contacted for the service.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). 

Milk containers in the North and South area refrigerators are observed without date marking and partially emptied. Food handler was consulted and stated that the containers were opened yesterday. Employee used a sharpie to mark yesterday's date on the containers. PIC is instructed to ensure that TCS foods held more than a day after opening are adequately marked.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) An in use wiping cloth was observed stored on a counter across from the oven. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. The cloth was moved to a bucket of sanitizer during the inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.11  (C)  Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair. 1) (REPEAT) A gap was observed around the mop sink in the utility room. The PIC was instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. 2) The caulking around the hand sink in the kitchen is observed cracking and in need of repair. PIC is instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) 3) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. The floor in the walk in cooler was observed with some food debris in the corners and along the wall edges. PIC is instructed to keep clean.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean equipment and utensils were observed being stored in a container that had an accumulation of debris in the bottom on the top shelf next to the walk in cooler. PIC was directed to the container and it (as well as the items inside it) were moved to the dish machine for cleaning.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11  (C) A gap was observed around the mop sink in the utility room. The PIC was instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) A bottle of lemonade was observed in the food prep area of the kitchen partially empty. PIC was directed to ensure that employee beverages in the food prep areas have a lid and straw so as to limit the hand/ mouth contact.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 (A) (3) (C) Single service items shall be stored at least 6 inches above the floor.

Observed packages of single service cups stored on the floor in the dry storage room. Discussed with the PIC and the items were moved to their designated location on a shelf.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

Two tags in the walk in cooler were observed to have a mold like substance on them. One was a tag on a shelf and the other a sign on the door to the walk in freezer. Once directed to the issue, the PIC removed the signs and had the locations cleaned by an employee.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

Observed multiple cans in dry storage to have significant dents along the seams. Cans with dents should be separated from those intended for use and returned to the supplier. Cans were set aside during the inspection and the person who receives the deliveries was instructed on the procedure.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

Observed a moist cloth to be stored out of solution during the inspection. Moist cloths should be stored in solution to prevent the growth of bacteria/mold. Cloth was moved for cleaning during the inspection.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.
Observed multiple phone chargers stored and plugged in next to ready to eat foods. Chargers were moved during the inspection. Also observed a coat stored next to bowls used for coking. Coat was moved to the chemical room during the inspection.
